description: V0.4 Wave 1 (V0.4-00 + V0.4-01 + V0.4-04 + V0.4-08): parallel development, serial integration. The Main Agent owns V0.4-00 (Desktop Development Preflight & Dev-Port Closure) on the shared worktree. Three Sub-Agents each own one bounded Runtime domain in its own isolated worktree: A = Recorder Control Plane & Session API (runtime/canx/recorder/**, the new runtime/canx/api/recorder.py, and the recorder mount seam in runtime/canx/api/app.py plus an observability seam in runtime/canx/runtime/service.py); B = Historical Signal Query + Downsampling Foundation (runtime/canx/query/** plus the new runtime/canx/plot/** domain package); C = Offline Replay Domain + Deterministic Scheduler (the new runtime/canx/replay/** domain package). Ownership surfaces are disjoint: B has no api/**, A has no query/plot/replay/**, C has no api/recorder/query write surface. All four branch from V0_4_WAVE1_BASE_SHA 127ee2ff3ba0600afc3c7826e879981ef0a64867. Integration order is fixed V0.4-00 -> V0.4-01 -> V0.4-04 -> V0.4-08, each rebased onto the new current main after the previous merge; no PR is merged before independent acceptance.

tasks.title: Desktop Development Preflight & Dev-Port Closure
tasks.objective: Close the V0.3 P2 accepted non-blocking defect where apps/desktop/src-tauri/tauri.conf.json declares devUrl http://localhost:1420 but apps/desktop/vite.config.ts does not pin the Vite dev server port, so pnpm tauri dev cannot reliably connect to the declared port. The fix is minimal and fail-closed: vite.config.ts must set server.port = 1420 and server.strictPort = true, so if 1420 is occupied Vite refuses to start rather than silently moving to 1421 while Tauri waits on 1420. No product architecture, Runtime API, recorder, Plot, Replay, dependency or proxy change is permitted. A regression guard (a machine-checkable contract test that reads the REAL configs, not a string grep) locks Tauri devUrl port == 1420 == Vite server.port and Vite strictPort == true going forward. A real pnpm tauri dev native smoke proves Vite listens on 1420, the Tauri dev shell and the CAN-X window start, the Runtime sidecar starts from the Desktop, /health and /runtime/status are reachable, the WebView loads the frontend, and closing the Desktop shuts the Runtime down without leaving an orphan canx-runtime or a stray Vite/Tauri process.
tasks.scope: apps/desktop/vite.config.ts and the Desktop preflight smoke/test surface, plus the V0.4-00 acceptance document.
non_goals: Any product architecture, Runtime API, recorder, Plot or Replay change
Any dependency, lockfile or package manifest change
Introducing a new dev server, a proxy workaround or an alternate port
Touching the Rust/Tauri source unless the real smoke proves it is required (and then only with a recorded reason)
acceptance_criteria: apps/desktop/vite.config.ts sets server.port = 1420 and server.strictPort = true
A machine-checkable test reads the real tauri.conf.json and vite.config.ts and asserts 1420 == 1420 and strictPort === true, so the two can never drift again
Tauri devUrl port and Vite server.port are proven equal by reading the configs, not by a substring grep
pnpm tauri dev starts Vite on 1420 and the Tauri window connects (recorded as a real native smoke, or explicitly NOT VERIFIED with the environment reason)
No file outside the allowed surface is modified
handoff_requirements: Report the exact command and result for the focused preflight test, pnpm test, pnpm typecheck, pnpm lint and pnpm build
Report the real pnpm tauri dev smoke evidence, or state explicitly that it could not run in this environment and why
State that no file outside allowed_paths was touched

tasks.title: Recorder Control Plane & Session API
tasks.objective: Upgrade the existing, mature recorder persistence/lifecycle (ProjectRecorder, DataSessionWriter, DataSessionService, the RuntimeService capture lifecycle, /capture/start, /capture/stop, /runtime/status) into an observable, queryable, session-based Recorder control plane, WITHOUT rewriting the recorder and WITHOUT creating a second recorder start/stop authority: the Capture Runtime still owns recording ingress lifecycle. Add a typed Recorder control/service model that can report active/inactive, stream identity, data_session_id, recorder lifecycle state, recorded frame count, failure, finalization pending/settled and durable session state; and a persisted session query surface that lists sessions in a validated CAN-X project, reads one session's durable metadata/state, distinguishes ACTIVE / COMPLETED / FAILED, rejects a nonexistent session, rejects an invalid project and returns bounded deterministic results. Only expose data that has durable authority; never scan all Parquet data to guess a value SQLite does not hold. Expose a typed, bounded, headless, UI-independent HTTP surface in a new runtime/canx/api/recorder.py, mounting it (and its typed error surface) into the existing runtime/canx/api/app.py without refactoring app.py. All SQLite/filesystem blocking work runs via asyncio.to_thread. Reuse DataSessionService / DataSessionWriter / ProjectService / SQLite metadata; do not copy SQLite query logic, Parquet integrity logic or session-state logic into the recorder module.

tasks.title: Historical Signal Query + Downsampling Foundation
tasks.objective: Build the bounded signal-series query and deterministic downsampling foundation a historical Plot will consume, on top of the existing persisted CAN DataSession + Query + DBC decode, WITHOUT creating a second historical data engine and WITHOUT building the Plot UI. Signal identity is never just a signal name: it carries channel_id, asset_id, message identity and signal identity, semantically consistent with the V0.3 realtime Plot SignalSelection, and two same-named signals on different channels are never merged into one series. The source of truth is Project -> registered DataSession -> verified Parquet segments -> QueryService / QueryEngine -> canonical Frame -> verified project-owned DBC -> DbcDecoder -> signal series; no frontend cache as authority, no loading a whole project into pandas, no loading a whole DataSession, no bypassing segment integrity, no globbing project files and assuming trust. Historical reads are paged/chunked/bounded/deterministic, so memory does not grow linearly with the dataset. Add a Runtime-side deterministic downsampling that maps a large dataset to a bounded PlotSample series preserving first point, last point and significant extrema better than a blind stride, with stable deterministic output, a strict maximum result bound and ordered timestamps. Streaming must use bounded page -> decode -> online/bucket aggregation -> discard, so working memory tracks page size + sample budget, not dataset size. Downsampling lives in the Runtime, not only the frontend; the realtime series.ts stride is not simply copied as the large-data answer.

tasks.title: Offline Replay Domain + Deterministic Scheduler
tasks.objective: Build CAN-X's first Replay domain, strictly OFFLINE. The source is a persisted DataSession; the output is an offline replay event/sink, never adapter.send(). This task must not add CanAdapter.send, python-can TX, hardware TX, a Safety Kernel authorization implementation, ARM state or a real bus replay; offline replay does not require TX authorization and real CAN replay (with a TX Safety Gate) is a later phase. Replay uses canonical recorded timing based on Frame.normalized_timestamp: relative_offset(frame_n) = normalized_timestamp(frame_n) - normalized_timestamp(first_frame), with speed defaulting to 1.0 (speed multiplier / pause / resume / step / loop / range belong to V0.4-09). A deterministic scheduler is built on an injectable clock abstraction (ReplayClock with monotonic() and sleep_until()/sleep()), with the production path using the real monotonic clock and tests using a fake clock, so deterministic tests never depend on asyncio.sleep(1.0) or wall-clock jitter. The same DataSession + replay configuration + clock behaviour must produce the same frame order, relative schedule, replay event order and terminal state. The canonical Frame is preserved in full (sequence, channel_id, arbitration_id, is_extended, is_fd, BRS, ESI, DLC, data, direction, timestamps, flags); offline replay never rebuilds an information-reduced Frame. Large sessions are read through the existing bounded QueryService pagination (DataSession -> bounded page -> scheduler -> sink -> next page), never loading a whole DataSession into memory. A minimal lifecycle is established: IDLE / RUNNING / COMPLETED / FAILED (an explicit STOPPED/CANCELLED may be added with stated semantics), with PAUSED / LOOPING / TRIGGER_WAIT left to later phases. The failure model covers an invalid project, an unknown session, a FAILED/incomplete session policy, a query failure, corrupted persisted data, a sink failure, a scheduler failure and cancellation, leaving no orphan replay task and never disguising a partial replay as COMPLETED.
